exposure: Blunt expansion of uterine incision during LSCS
Sharp expansion of uterine incision during LSCS
outcome: Intraoperative blood loss (changes in hematocrit, hemoglobin, red blood cell count)
cohort: A total of 120 pregnant women undergoing lower segment cesarean section were randomly assigned to two groups.
finding: Blunt expansion of the uterine incision during LSCS resulted in significantly lower intraoperative blood loss compared to sharp expansion.
mod_finding: Blunt expansion of the uterine incision during cesarean deliveries is a preferable technique to minimize blood loss.
